kills.flaw: Revenue starts at month 10 or later and depends on an unreleased Bandai game not flopping. The customer's profit shows up more than a year out, which fails the 12-month $5-10k goal by design. The $10-15 RPM on borrowed Piltover traffic is a guess, and Bandai can ship its own official database.

Its own author says it misses the goal (about $1.5-2k/mo net at month 12). Customers are hard to reach 45+ collectors who see free apps as good enough, and the real payoff is consignment years out. It is a long-dated option, not a business for a solo operator with $5-25k.

A $55 gross margin against a ~$38 Meta cost per purchase leaves about $17-25 per order. It needs about 250 orders a month to matter and only reaches that in Q4. Pokemon trademark rules limit the ad creative, and a competitor can copy the offer in a weekend. The unit economics don't hold once ad costs are paid.

upgrades.upgrade: Make it the default desk and add business-2's third route. Leads below your buy threshold get referred to partner shops for a 10% finder's fee, so even junk-wax leads help pay for the ads. Consign any lot over $3k by default: the seller is paid after the sale, so you never front cash and the deal size isn't limited by your bankroll. Copy Dean's Cards' bid-software discipline (about 1,000 collections a year, 80%+ offer acceptance) by having Claude build a fixed offer rubric, so a stranger with a checklist can produce the same offer.

Put the 'we show you the receipts' comp report into the leverage-1 funnel as the closer. Keep the 24-hour estimate free, but gate the full itemized report behind a booked call or a ship-in, so tire-kickers screen themselves out before the user spends any time.
Show the cash and consign offers side by side in every reply. Add a rule that consign is the default above $3k, so trust converts the big lots without tying up working capital.

Make its $8k bankroll cap, its day-90 kill rule (net under $250 per buy or fewer than 8 buys) and its maximum designed loss of about $2.5k the guardrails for whichever collection-desk variant wins. This is a guardrail set, not a separate business.

Don't pay 55-65% just because appraisal is now cheap. Sell speed and transparency, and keep buys at 50-55% so the 30%+ margin cushion survives a falling comp. Delay the $1k+ scanner until you are past 6 buys a month.

Add a ladder. Start with a $299 prepaid 'Q4 Amazon ad audit for card-accessory brands' as the front-end offer, then a $1,500/mo retainer with a 3-month minimum, first month prepaid. Widen the target list beyond Amazon brands to Shopify card-supply stores, grading-supply and display-case brands running Google and Meta, because 50-150 reachable Amazon brands is too thin a pool.

Merge with business-mind-2 and first-principles-3 into one shop-lead product sold as prepaid credit packs (for example 10 photo-qualified sellers for $1,000, paid upfront), with ad spend on the shop's own card. That gives negative working capital and ends the 'that lead didn't show' billing disputes. Sell it only for leads outside the user's own buying radius.

Feed the show from the collection desk. Put a 'Free AI appraisal + cash offer' booth at the door and add a VIP early-entry ticket ($15-20). Run the founding-vendor pre-sale (25 paid tables by day 15 or refund everyone) before signing any venue contract, so customers fund the event.

Merge with business-3 into one 'card seller ads desk' with a $149 paid audit as the front end. Lead with eBay's Jan-2026 Promoted Listings attribution leak, which is measurable and can be priced as a share of savings. Whatnot Boost alone is too thin a lever to retain clients.
Run it only as a Q4 bolt-on that turns bulk from the collection desk into cash. Pre-sell the Starter Kit SKU before buying the 20k-card bulk lot, and stop on Dec 20.
Charge a $299 setup fee plus a monthly minimum before any rev share. Aged stock is often aged because it is overpriced, so 10% of GMV alone may never cover the user's sales time.

combo: Prepaid Supply Machine. (1) Core: the leverage-1 collection desk in the home metro, with marketing-1's receipts-first comp report as the closer and business-2's three routes. Buy at 50-55%, consign above $3k (seller paid after the sale, so no capital is tied up), and refer below-threshold leads to shops for 10%. It runs under mindset-2's $8k bankroll cap and day-90 kill rule. (2) Overflow: leads outside the user's radius are sold to shops as prepaid credit packs (marketing-3, business-mind-2 and first-principles-3 merged), so that leg has negative working capital. (3) From month 3-4: a vendor-prepaid monthly show (business-1) that also works as a free intake booth for the desk. (4) In Q4 only, desk bulk becomes demand-2 gift bundles. Every leg either gets paid first or turns cash in under 45 days, and none needs card prices to rise. Honest middle: about $5-7k/mo by month 12.
message: Eight of us independently proposed the same profit pool: buying from non-hobbyist sellers with paid search plus AI triage. That convergence is the signal, so let's stop debating whether to do it and pick the variant with the best cash cycle. Mine is leverage-1 plus consign-by-default plus refer-out, because it fixes the two things that kill this model: capital limits and junk-wax CAC. Bolt on only pieces that get paid first (shop lead credit packs, vendor-prepaid shows), and kill anything whose payoff is a year out.
